entries.finding: a TLS upload is not checked against the server name

Refusing would block installing a certificate for a new name before DNS and server_name move, or on a host reached by address

entries.source: prod deploy v1.2.0 on .90, 2026-09-30
entries.finding: The FULL online upgrade (upgrade-full.sh with --repo-url, no --audit-only/--backup-only) does not print the final 'RESULT: exit N' line promised by round 7 (M1); --audit-only and --backup-only do. README/INSTALL tell the operator to read `tail -n 1` of the log, which on the full run shows the Rollback line instead.
entries.where: install/upgrade-full.sh (the full-run exit path after the post-upgrade checklist)
entries.repro: prod .90: /root/tm-upgrade-1.2.0-full.log ends with 'Rollback: sudo bash /root/tm-v1.2.0/install/upgrade-full.sh --restore 20260930-033204', no RESULT line; t47 covers the doc/script agreement but not this exit path.
entries.closes_when: a t47 case runs the full-upgrade exit path and asserts the last line is RESULT: exit 0
entries.root_cause: install/upgrade-full.sh:3252 `trap - EXIT` on the success path disables the handler that prints RESULT; confirmed on tm-qc (both offline upgrades) and prod (online).
entries.fixed: v1.2.1 (WO-0005), commit 07264b0 on release/v1.2.1 (unreleased until the v1.2.1 tag): the success path re-arms the result-only trap (trap 'result_line "$?"' EXIT) instead of `trap - EXIT`, so every exit ends with RESULT: exit <N> and a failure after completion still does not roll back. closes_when met: t47 a-successful-full-upgrade-ends-with-result-exit-0 runs the REAL tail of the script behind the real _on_exit (online and --offline end with RESULT: exit 0; a post-completion failure ends with RESULT: exit 7 and no rollback); mutation controls M603-M607.
entries.disposition: fixed in v1.2.1

entries.source: prod deploy v1.2.0 on .90, 2026-09-30

Host configuration, not the product; the upgrade could mask or ignore the sssd socket units in its post-check, or document it.

entries.source: WO-0006 assure-fix-1 (builder, 2026-10-03)

entries.source: WO-0006 assure-fix-2 (builder, 2026-10-03); POLICY QUESTION FOR JAMES

Their release commits lay down subsets of LEGACY_ARTEFACTS (1.0.0: unit, wants link, site, sites-enabled link; +logrotate from 1.0.2; +header snippet 1.0.3; +nginx-test unit and polkit rule 1.0.4/1.0.5), and tm/VERSION 1.0.0 is reported by 1.0.0, 1.0.1 and the 1.0.2 release commit 29671b1.
entries.closes_when: per-version shipped lists for 1.0.0-1.0.5, each re-derived by t45 from a named, immutable reference (tag the release commits, or pin their 40-hex ids), and a rollback case per list; or a decision that pre-1.0.6 hosts are out of support

entries.finding: On a 1.0.x host where a v1.3.0 upgrade already failed and rolled back, v1.3.0's rollback put back the unit, site, snippet and logrotate file from its legacy copies but NOT topic-manager-nginx-test.service or the polkit rule (it kept no copy of either). A v1.3.1 restore point on that host records those two as found (the 1.3.0 bytes) because nothing holds the 1.0.x bytes, so a later rollback puts the 1.3.0 versions back. The rest of the leftovers (socket, apply/audit units, helper tree, log format) are retired. README 'Upgrading from a 1.0.x host' says to revert the snapshot taken before that attempt.
entries.where: backup_owned_artefacts (derived record: 'as found on this host')
entries.closes_when: the 1.0.x bytes of those two files can be reconstructed from the release (e.g. the tag's file, with the installer's edits) and compared, or the throwaway re-test confirms the snapshot-revert guidance is enough and the entry is accepted

entries.finding: Declared gate sca is RED: Werkzeug 3.1.8 (requirements.txt and requirements.lock) carries GHSA-g6x2-hccm-hh4m / CVE-2026-102598, MODERATE (CVSS 4.0 AV:N/AC:L/AT:P ... VA:L), CWE-67: safe_join() accepts Windows special device names; fixed in 3.1.9. GitHub-reviewed 2026-10-05, after v1.3.0 shipped, so v1.3.0 is affected too.
